sections.Overview:
Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites predominantly in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, the U.K., Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Sweden, Iceland, and New Zealand, with 939 warehouses worldwide as of August 30, 2026 [10-K accession 0000909832-26-000093, line L000734]. Its business model centers on providing a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products at low prices through a membership format, driving high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover that yields operational efficiency [10-K L000737]. The company sources merchandise primarily from direct suppliers, routing goods through cross-docking depots for efficient distribution to warehouses, with e-commerce operations integrated into this supply system [10-K L000738-L000741]. Average warehouse space is approximately 148,000 square feet, designed for merchandising efficiency and inventory control, operating under a no-frills, self-service structure to limit overhead costs [10-K L000742]. Membership fees, including $65 annual base fees in the U.S., contribute to revenues and include Executive memberships with rewards incentives [10-K L000773-L000782]. In 2026, Costco's merchandise offerings span core categories of foods and sundries, non-foods, fresh foods, warehouse ancillary services such as gasoline and pharmacy, and complementary businesses like e-commerce and travel [10-K L000746-L000763].

Insight: Costco's California operations alone comprised 26% of U.S. net sales in 2026, underscoring a significant geographic concentration risk that could materially affect overall financial performance if that market experiences downturns [10-K L000837].
sections.Market Positioning and Growth Outlook: Costco differentiates competitively through its membership warehouse format focusing on low prices supported by high volumes and inventory turnover, controlled selection of fast-moving SKUs (less than 4,000 per warehouse), and efficient, streamlined warehouse design [10-K L000737, L000744]. The membership renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026, indicating strong customer loyalty [10-K L000783]. Executive memberships accounted for approximately 42,300 thousand paid members in 2026 and drove about 75.2% of worldwide net sales [10-K L000782]. The company operated 939 warehouses globally, with 647 in the U.S. and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, and others across multiple international markets, reflecting broad geographic diversification [EX-99.1 L000021]. Catalysts for growth include warehouse expansion in existing and new markets, with attention to navigating local regulatory and competitive environments [10-K L000838-L000841].
sections.Valuation Insights:
Costco Wholesale Corporation reported total revenue for fiscal year ended August 30, 2026, of $303.154 billion [C:r1], representing a year-over-year growth of 10.1% [C:g1]. Operating income was $11.685 billion [C:oi1], yielding an operating margin of approximately 3.85% [C:om1]. Net income attributable to the company was $9.226 billion [C:ni1]. GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) amounted to $20.76 [C:eps1]. Return on average equity (ROE) reached 28.4% [C:roe1]. Total debt, including current portion, sums to $6.163 billion against equity of $35.803 billion, giving a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.172 [C:debt1]. Free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures) stood at $9.382 billion [C:fcf1]. Latest quarterly revenue data and GAAP diluted EPS for the quarter are Not established from the given release lines and exhibits. Based on the closing price of $904.70 on 2026-09-23, the price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 43.58 [C:pe1]. 

Peer operating margins on a consistent total revenue definition for the comparable fiscal periods are: Walmart Inc. at 4.18% [C:wmtoi], Target Corp. at 4.88% [C:tgtom], and BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. at 3.81% [C:bjom]. The margin comparison shows Costco’s margin is below Walmart and Target but slightly above BJ's.

Sources follow strict GAAP and XBRL tagging to ensure comparability. The revenue figure is from the tag RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax which is explicitly identified as total revenue, not net sales.

Insight: The company's long-term debt excluding current portion decreased from $5.713 billion at August 31, 2025, to $3.914 billion at August 30, 2026, indicating a significant reduction in noncurrent liabilities over the fiscal year [C:debt_lt]. This finding is from the 10-K filing accession 0000909832-26-000093, line L000085, designated L000123.
sections.Future Developments and Strategic Recomm: Costco plans to continue opening warehouses both in existing markets to increase share and in new markets where brand recognition and member acquisition present challenges [10-K L000838-L000841]. The company also pursues diversification and expansion of its supply chain, including expanding in-country production and private-label merchandise, to enhance control over merchandise and value [10-K L000768]. Monitoring the risks related to geographic concentration, especially U.S. and Canadian operations which represented 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income respectively in 2026, is critical for strategic decisions [10-K L000836-L000837]. Investments in e-commerce and warehouse ancillary services should continue to support member convenience and attract frequent shopping [10-K L000767].
sections.Investment Recommendation:
Hold provisional, based on the operating margin of 3.85% [C:om1] which is lower than Walmart's 4.18% and Target's 4.88%, showing mixed margin competitiveness relative to peers.

Insight: The company's long-term debt excluding current portion decreased from $5.713 billion at August 31, 2025, to $3.914 billion at August 30, 2026, indicating a significant reduction in noncurrent liabilities over the fiscal year [C:debt_lt] as reported in the 10-K filing, line L000085 designated L000123.

COSTCO WHOLESALE CORPORATION REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FISCAL YEAR 2026 OPERATING RESULTS
ISSAQUAH, Wash., September 24, 2026 - Costco Wholesale Corporation (“Costco” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: COST) today announced its operating results for the 16-week fourth quarter and the 52-week fiscal year ended August 30, 2026.
Net sales for the quarter increased 11.2 percent, to $93.9 billion, from $84.4 billion last year. Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year.
Comparable sales for the fourth quarter and fiscal year were as follows:
| 16 Weeks |  | 16 Weeks |  | 52 Weeks |  | 52 Weeks
|  |  | Adjusted* |  |  |  | Adjusted*
U.S. | 10.7% |  | 7.2% |  | 8.2% |  | 6.6%
Canada | 5.0% |  | 4.6% |  | 7.8% |  | 6.7%
Other International | 7.0% |  | 6.2% |  | 9.8% |  | 6.5%
Total Company | 9.4% |  | 6.7% |  | 8.4% |  | 6.6%
Digitally-Enabled | 19.5% |  | 19.8% |  | 20.9% |  | 20.7%
*Excluding the impacts from changes in gasoline prices and foreign exchange.
Net income for the fourth quarter was $2.998 billion, $6.75 per diluted share, compared to $2.610 billion, $5.87 per diluted share, last year. This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values. Net income for the fiscal year was $9.226 billion, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8.099 billion, $18.21 per diluted share, last year.
Costco currently operates 939 warehouses, including 647 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 115 in Canada, 43 in Mexico, 37 in Japan, 29 in the United Kingdom, 20 in Korea, 15 in Australia, 14 in Taiwan, seven in China, five in Spain, three in France, two in Sweden, and one each in Iceland, and New Zealand. Costco also operates e-commerce sites in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Mexico, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Australia, and China.
A conference call to discuss these results is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. (PT) today, September 24, 2026, and will be available via a webcast on investor.costco.com (click “Events & Presentations”).
